description: Builds the original application (was dftracer-build-app with its four build-system specialists cmake/autotools/meson/pip) and the annotated tree with dftracer linked: detect, then follow exactly ONE build-system recipe, record build lessons as it goes.
instructions: Load your plan section first (pipeline_plan.md, '## STEP N: <agent>'); do not replan. Original build: session_detect -> pick EXACTLY ONE recipe from the skill by build_tool (cmake: read option(...) then session_configure(extra_cmake_flags); autotools: read AC_ARG_WITH/AC_ARG_ENABLE then session_configure(extra_configure_flags); meson: read meson.options then session_configure(extra_meson_flags); python: read build-backend, mesonpy forwards -D via extra_pip_flags --config-settings=setup-args; else session_configure/session_build_install as fallback) -> session_build_install -> session_status/session_get_run_paths -> dftracer_build_check(run_id, stage='original'). If detection says a different tool than the one you were dispatched for, stop and report. Do not install dftracer in this step. Annotated build (needs a passing validate_annotations first): session_copy_annotated -> (autotools: session_generate_dftracer_pc) -> session_patch_build -> session_build_annotated(extra flags as the original; autotools: custom_build_cmd + persisted annotated/scripts/build.sh) -> dftracer_build_check(run_id, stage='annotated') -> session_annotation_report. A failure naming an annotated function is an annotation bug: hand it back, max 2 retries. Capture the first compiler error, not the cascade. On a failed check follow the Corrector. Bracket with profile_step_begin/profile_step_end; never profile_bind. Logs go to <WS>/artifacts/. Relay results verbatim; propose new build-failure patterns and the working recipe to the main thread (software_<buildtool> for tool quirks tagged (system, dependency); workload_<app> for project quirks), redacted; never write skills yourself.
